newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia welcomes decision by Serbian parliament.
newsitem.headline: Russia welcomes decision by Serbian parliament.

text.p: Russia welcomed on Wednesday the Serbian parliament's approval of a law reinstating opposition victories in local elections and said it provided a chance for national reconciliation.
"This decision by the Serbian parliament, promoting national reconciliation, is welcomed in Moscow," the foreign ministry said in a statement.
"The legal basis has thus been created for a political way out of the protracted confrontation between the authorities and the opposition."

The Serbian parliament's decision on Tuesday reversed the ruling Socialists' decision to annul opposition victories by the Zajedno (Together) coalition last November in 14 cities, including Belgrade. They had complained of "irregularities".
The refusal to recognise the opposition victories had prompted weeks of protests in Belgrade and caused an international outcry.
Russia is a long-time ally of autocratic Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and had not officially taken sides in the dispute.
The foreign ministry said it was now important that broad discussion starts on the problems on the way to further "democratisation".
It called for a halt to mass protests and an easing of tension, and said the two sides should avoid making new demands and mutual accusations.
Zoran Djindjic, one of the three leaders of Zajedno, said on Wednesday he expected the protests to continue until "larger changes" were made in Serbia.
